title: Machine-Checked Algebraic Kernel and Exact-Rational Certificates for Prime-Power Finite Differences, Fourier Rounding, CRT, and Periodic-Fourier NMQC_oplus Torus Approximations
abstract: Shuhei Osaki and Ryuhei Mori (arXiv:2611.32163, November 24, 2026) resolved the optimal torus-polynomial degree of AND_n/2 at O(log(n/eps)) (improving O(log^2(n/eps))), sharpened depth-d, size-s AC^0[m] torus degree to C_m^d (log s)^(max{1,mu-1} d) log(1/eps), and proved equivalence between r-parity periodic Fourier representations (NMQC_oplus) and degree-O(log(r/eps)) torus polynomials. We deliver an explicitly scoped, zero-floating-point verification stack for the deterministic algebraic, finite-difference, Fourier-rounding, CRT, and periodic-Fourier conversion mechanisms of this result. First, an 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4.35.0 kernel (TorusACC0.lean; 0 sorry, 0 warnings, 0 Classical.choice; 3 zero-axiom, 1 [propext], 14 [propext, Quot.sound]) proves universal algebraic identities and inductive bounds—including universal mod-8 congruence for Lemma 9 (q=2, k=3) over all z in Nat, universal coprime CRT factorization delta_{q1*q2}(z) = delta_{q1}(z)*delta_{q2}(z) for all gcd(q1,q2)=1, Appendix B exact prime-power degree (p-1)p^{e-1}k + p^{e-1} - 1 <= (q-1)k, Beigel-Tarui degree domination, Lemma 11 composite degree recurrence, inductive Theorem 14 rounding-sum bounds, and exact integer-cleared rational square checks supporting Fact 19 under the external bracket 314/100 < pi < 355/113. Second, TORUS-ACC0-CERT-1.0 audits 16 canonical exact-Q witnesses (0.129-3.911 ms)—including full-period [0, P-1] Lemma 9 certification proving congruence for all z in Z—and rejects 60/60 live adversarial forgeries.
